Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: No evidence of business registration/licensing integration with government data exchange. Services are largely paper-based.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score and 'largely paper-based' comment are outdated; the cited World Bank PDF gave no sector-specific evidence. Fresh evidence shows the Burundi Revenue Authority (OBR) launched a web-based Guichet Unique Électronique (GUE) in February 2026 that operationally interconnects OBR, the medicines/food regulator ABREMA and the ASYCUDA World customs system for import and licensing permits, alongside an existing online tax e-filing/e-payment portal (e-KORI) and an online company-registration portal (easybusiness.bi). This is genuine cross-agency data exchange, though not yet covering all business-registration and tax functions in one system. Recalculated from 0 to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Burundi has multiple digitised and partially interlinked systems for business and licensing administration. The Office Burundais des Recettes (OBR) launched a web-based Guichet Unique Électronique (GUE) in February 2026 that operationally connects OBR, the pharmaceuticals/food regulator ABREMA and the ASYCUDA World customs platform, letting importers obtain permits, track applications and pay fees online with automatic data-sharing between agencies. OBR also runs an online tax declaration and payment portal (e-KORI/Umutangakori), and company registration is available via the easybusiness.bi online portal. Full integration across company registration, licensing and tax compliance has not yet been achieved.

revised_comments: Burundi's Ministry of National Education and Scientific Research operates an Education Management Information System (EMIS) that produces detailed annual statistical yearbooks, but a 2024 Global Partnership for Education assessment finds it is not integrated with other education data sources such as human resources management, infrastructure or examinations records. A June 2026 African Union technical workshop is helping Burundi self-assess its EMIS against continental norms and standards as a first step towards a future strengthening strategy, indicating that integration remains at an early planning stage.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: No evidence of health information system integration with a government interoperability platform. The country's digital infrastructure is nascent per World Bank.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original generic World Bank PDF did not support the score. Since October 2023, UNICEF has supported an interoperability pilot linking civil registry and health services in Kirundo province (52 health facilities), enabling birth registration at the point of immunisation. Separately, a national technical workshop (reported 2026) is developing interoperability standards (HL7 FHIR) to unify fragmented health platforms (DHIS2, SIDAInfo, OpenClinic) under the National Health Information Development Plan (PNDIS II, 2026-2028), with no public timeline yet. Recalculated from 0 to 3 (Under development): active but partial, province-limited integration work is under way.
revised_comments: Burundi is actively developing health-system interoperability. Since October 2023, a UNICEF-supported pilot has linked civil registry and health services in Kirundo province, allowing children to be registered and receive birth certificates directly at health facilities during vaccination visits. Separately, the Ministry of Public Health, under its National Health Information Development Plan (PNDIS II, 2026-2028), is working to make fragmented health platforms (DHIS2, SIDAInfo, OpenClinic) interoperable using the HL7 FHIR standard, though no public timeline or budget has been confirmed. Integration remains partial and province-limited rather than national.

Definition: Integration of driver's license registration and traffic offence data
Comments: No evidence of driver licensing system integration with government data exchange. No relevant sources found.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original claim of 'no relevant sources found' was incorrect. Burundi has issued biometric driving licences since 2016, and as of December 2025 a centralised digital platform is being deployed to interconnect the National Police, transport operator OTRACO, insurers, the revenue authority (OBR), telecoms and the judicial police, enabling real-time verification of licences, insurance and vehicle status. As of October 2025, biometric licence issuance itself was disrupted by a card shortage. Recalculated from 0 to 3 (Under development): an interoperable platform is being built and piloted, not yet fully operational.
revised_comments: Burundi has issued biometric driving licences since 2016. As of late 2025, the Ministry of Finance and the National Police were deploying a centralised digital platform, linked to a geographic information system, intended to interconnect the police, transport regulator OTRACO, insurers, the Office Burundais des Recettes and telecom operators, enabling real-time verification of licences, insurance, technical control and vehicle status, with citizen-facing tools for fine payment via mobile money. Rollout of biometric card production has faced supply disruptions.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: No evidence of social protection/grant registries integrated with government data exchange. Services are largely paper-based per World Bank.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The 'largely paper-based' comment is now outdated. Burundi operates CORE-MIS (built on openIMIS), an open-source social-protection management information system underpinning the Merankabandi cash-transfer programme, having migrated over one million beneficiary records, and is building a Unified Social Registry to consolidate demographic/socioeconomic data for cross-sector targeting. CORE-MIS explicitly supports interoperability with payment-service-provider and ID-database systems, and has been used for national shock response (2024 floods) and refugee programming with WFP/UNHCR/FAO. Recalculated from 0 to 4 (Partially integrated): nationwide and cross-agency in practice, though the fully unified registry across all social programmes is still being built.
revised_comments: Burundi's social protection system runs on CORE-MIS, an open-source management information system (built on openIMIS) that underpins the nationwide Merankabandi cash-transfer programme, covering around 1.5 million beneficiaries with over a million individual records migrated from the legacy system. CORE-MIS is designed for interoperability with payment-service-provider systems and identity databases, and the government is developing a Unified Social Registry to consolidate demographic and vulnerability data for cross-programme targeting spanning health, education, social protection and labour. The system has already supported national shock response, identifying over 100,000 flood-affected households in 2024, and coordination with humanitarian partners including the World Food Programme, UNHCR and the Food and Agriculture Organization for refugee caseloads.

revised_comments: Burundi validated a national Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025-2030) in April 2026, led by the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy with UNDP support, structured around six pillars including governance, infrastructure and human capital. The strategy foresees around 15 pilot projects in sectors such as health and agriculture (diagnostic support tools, telemedicine, climate alerts, farm advisory services), and the Bank of the Republic of Burundi is separately exploring AI for financial supervision and fraud detection. No AI capability has yet been deployed within a government data exchange system for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics; the strategy remains at the planning and early-pilot-design stage.
